_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH — edit only this file. All components read from it.

vulnbox.note: ssh_user/ssh_port = team patch key, only reaches this team's public-proxy container (no tcpdump there). capture_ssh_alias = admin SSH (via ~/.ssh/config, ProxyJump to gameserver) used by deploy-capture-pull.sh to tcpdump on the docker HOST. capture_iface (default "eth0"/auto) is the EXTERNAL interface, captured pre-NAT so each service's public port (services[].port) is what both tcpdump's BPF and Tulip see directly -- no docker_bridge / capture_port NAT workaround needed. Set docker_bridge only if eth0 genuinely is not where the public IP lives (rare; auto mode tries ip route first).

monitor_host.bind_ip_note: Address the control-plane ports (dashboard, redis, tulip, postgres) listen on. 127.0.0.1 = only this machine (safe default: the monitor host sits on the competition VPN, and these ports have no auth). Set to a LAN IP only to let teammates on a trusted network open the dashboard. The honeytoken port always listens on all interfaces by design.

flag.note: PUT with header X-Team-Token: <team token, kept OUT of this file — see team-tokens.txt locally>

gameserver_hint.note: ForcAD scoreboard; PUT /flags with X-Team-Token header to submit

honeytoken.note: a fake flag placed in a trap file on the vulnbox; if seen outbound it means compromise

tulip.note: Tulip stores flows in TimescaleDB/Postgres, not Mongo

mock_vulnbox.note: false = real vulnbox (DFCD practice arena, team-01). bringup.sh skips the toy app + ctf_proxy when false.

ctf_proxy.note: keyword MUST stay the single source other tools read from — do not hardcode elsewhere

ml_classifier.note: Do NOT enable during contest unless BTC has confirmed in writing; encoder/clustering classifier only, never generative. This flag has NO EFFECT when MODE=contest regardless of its value — bringup.sh never passes docker-compose.prep.yml (where ml-fingerprint lives) in contest mode, full stop. Only meaningful when MODE=prep.

services.name: web
services.note: team-03 public-proxy -> DFCD app stack (php/ws/mathsays). Capture is now on the external interface (pre-NAT), so port 8003 (the public port) is what both tcpdump and Tulip see directly -- no capture_port override needed. compose_service = the docker-compose service name on the vulnbox backing this port, used by deploy-ctfproxy.sh/hostagent to insert ctf_proxy per-service (falls back to ctf_proxy.insertion.remote_compose_service when a service entry omits this, for single-service configs written before this field existed).

retention.note: host_agent deletes captured pcaps in traffic/ (oldest first) only when needed: traffic/ grows past pcap_max_gb, or the disk has less than min_free_gb free. pcap_keep_minutes > 0 additionally deletes anything older than that (0 = off). Files younger than 10 min are never touched. Flows already imported stay in Tulip. On the vulnbox, pcaps are removed as soon as they are pulled. If min_free_gb is still violated after pcap cleanup, host_agent next prunes Docker's own dangling images/build-cache (always safe -- see contest-runtime/hostagent/retention.py). tulip_flow_retention_hours is a LAST-RESORT, opt-in-only escalation beyond that: 0 (default) = never touch Tulip's own flow data; set to e.g. 8 to let host_agent drop TimescaleDB chunks older than that many hours if disk is still critically low after everything else -- this deletes real captured contest flows, so leave it 0 unless you understand that tradeoff.
